title: P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II): John 15:2-16:4 (pages 110-115)
source: Papyrus Bodmer II (P66), Fondation Martin Bodmer: images from the Bodmer Lab, University of Geneva; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P66; English from the King James Version
description: John 15:2-16:4 in P66 (Papyrus Bodmer II), the papyrus codex of John copied around 200: pages 110-115, each with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P66 is a papyrus codex of the Gospel of John copied in Egypt around 200, the most complete early copy of John. Most of it is Papyrus Bodmer II in the Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny (Geneva); small pieces are in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin, and the Institut für Altertumskunde, Cologne. The first five quires (John 1:1-14:26) survive as a bound book of numbered pages; later leaves, from John 14:29 to 21:9, are damaged and kept between glass. The scribe made many corrections, some of them his own; only the first hand is shown here.

Each section below is one page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on the page. Pages of the bound book are shown on the photographic plates published by Victor Martin and J. W. B. Barns in 1962 (scanned by the Bodmer Lab), the glass-mounted leaves on colour photographs. Lost: John 6:12-34 (pages 35-38) and parts of chapters 14-21; the transcription ends at 21:9. Where P66 lacks a verse that the KJV has (John 5:4, the account of the adulteress at 7:53-8:11, 16:15), the section says so.

This entry covers pages 110-115 (John 15:2-16:4).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>15:2</sup>Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. <sup>3</sup>Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. <sup>4</sup>Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.

translation.text: <sup>15:4</sup>Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. <sup>5</sup>I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. <sup>6</sup>If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. <sup>7</sup>If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.

translation.text: <sup>15:7</sup>If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. <sup>8</sup>Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples. <sup>9</sup>As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love. <sup>10</sup>If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love. <sup>11</sup>These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full. <sup>12</sup>This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you. <sup>13</sup>Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

translation.text: <sup>15:13</sup>Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. <sup>14</sup>Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you. <sup>15</sup>Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you. <sup>16</sup>Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you. <sup>17</sup>These things I command you, that ye love one another. <sup>18</sup>If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. <sup>19</sup>If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.

translation.text: <sup>15:19</sup>If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. <sup>20</sup>Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also. <sup>21</sup>But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me. <sup>22</sup>If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin. <sup>23</sup>He that hateth me hateth my Father also. <sup>24</sup>If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father. <sup>25</sup>But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.

translation.text: <sup>15:25</sup>But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause. <sup>26</sup>But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me: <sup>16:2</sup>They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service. <sup>3</sup>And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me. <sup>4</sup>But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you.
